clue.text: The spirit of endless protest

definitions.note: marc is a brandy distilled from grape pressings

indicators.note: endless says the protest word loses its final letter

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration

explanation.surface: A wistful line about the essence of a campaign that never stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a strong brandy made from the residue of pressed grapes, a kind of spirit.

clue.text: Friend about to make changes to plan

indicators.note: about means around, so the friend word surrounds the changes word

parts.note: mate is a friend
to edit is to make changes to text

explanation.surface: A pal is about to revise the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'going to'; 'about' alone is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate can mean to plan or intend, as in meditating revenge.

clue.text: Relax in park, joining queue

parts.note: rec, short for recreation ground, is a British word for a park
a line is a queue

explanation.surface: Taking it easy in a park after joining a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec is a public recreation ground, a British local park.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lean back and rest, a way of relaxing.

clue.text: Transatlantic thoroughfare terminates unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters of terminates turn up in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A road in America comes to a sudden end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transatlantic' marks the term as American: the chief street of a US town.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the principal street of a town, the equivalent of the British high street.

clue.text: Getting rid of a cross in front of graveyard

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

indicators.note: front of means the first letter of graveyard

explanation.surface: Removing a cross that stands before a cemetery.
explanation.definitionFit: Axing is cutting or dismissing, eliminating something entirely.

clue.text: Club near to quiet street? The reverse

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: The reverse says the words to quiet street are read backwards

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical sign for quiet

explanation.surface: Is the club near a quiet street, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse' turns TOPST into TSPOT after NIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is an entertainment venue open late, also called a club.

clue.text: Chief is regularly stroppy

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of stroppy is taken

explanation.surface: A boss who keeps losing their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Top as an adjective means highest-ranking or principal, the same as chief.

clue.text: Interpret old poet

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Ezra Pound was an American poet

explanation.surface: Explain the work of an ancient bard.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to set out or explain in detail, a way of interpreting.

clue.text: Little brat ultimately irritating

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of brat

parts.note: itchy means causing irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: A small child who ends up being annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: Titchy is informal British for very small.
explanation.definitionFit: Titchy is colloquial British for tiny, from the music-hall comic Little Tich.

clue.text: I'm wanting cheap-sounding accommodation, having no regrets

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: the hyphenated sounding says the word for cheap is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a penny is a coin of trifling value, so cheap; said aloud it gives the start of the word for sorry
a tent is camping accommodation

explanation.surface: A camper who cannot afford better lodging says they are not sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheap-sounding' gives PENI, heard as 'penny'; 'wanting' just joins I'M to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To be impenitent is to be unrepentant, feeling no remorse.

clue.text: Leaving magic pen to be repaired by daughter

indicators.note: something to be repaired will be put back together differently, so the letters of magic pen are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes a broken magic pen to their daughter for fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' puts D beside the anagram ECAMPING of MAGIC PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Decamping is departing suddenly or secretly, a form of leaving.

clue.text: Spot Italian songster

parts.note: a pip is a spot, as on dice or playing cards
IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in vermouth

explanation.surface: Pick out a singer from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipit is a small songbird, and songster is an old word for a singing bird.

clue.text: Rhubarb is something to eat

definitions.meaning: rhubarb is British slang for nonsense or meaningless chatter
the stomach lining of cattle, eaten as food

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhubarb' looks like the food; it is the nonsense sense, while the second half gives the edible one.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: tripe means rubbish talk, and is also cooked cow stomach.

clue.text: Suffer, as one having tour of factory might?

definitions.meaning: to endure a hard and gruelling experience

definitions.text: one having tour of factory might
definitions.meaning: a visitor to a works literally passes through the building where grinding is done

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the idiom literally: a factory visitor walks round the mill.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to undergo hardship or a punishing ordeal, while a mill is also a factory.

clue.text: Engineers, men entering building likely to be refurbished

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: entering puts the men inside the building word

parts.note: a stable is a building for horses
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Engineers go into a building that could be renovated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restorable can be repaired and brought back to good condition.

clue.text: See 13
Adulating one with pride, I burst into song

indicators.note: burst into means the letter pushes its way inside

parts.note: a group of lions is a pride
sing means to make song

explanation.surface: Someone full of pride breaks into song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' looks like self-esteem; it is a group of lions. 'burst into song' reads as an idiom, but the I bursts into the middle of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To lionise is to treat someone as a celebrity, heaping adulation on them.

clue.text: Flat can accommodate sailor, wanting a place to stay in Cadiz?

indicators.note: accommodate means hold within, so the sailor goes inside the flat

parts.note: pad is slang for a flat or home
OS is ordinary seaman, a common abbreviation for a sailor

explanation.surface: A flat can take in a seaman who needs somewhere to stay in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting a' says the result still needs an A at the end. The question mark flags a definition by example: Cadiz is a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: A posada is a Spanish inn or lodging house, somewhere to stay in a Spanish city.

clue.text: First of these decrees surprisingly kept hidden

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters come out in an unexpected order
First of means the opening letter of these

explanation.surface: Official orders that were unexpectedly withheld from the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Secreted, past tense of secrete, means stashed away or concealed.

clue.text: Sword too light to be carried?

indicators.note: something carried is held within, so the light word sits inside too

parts.note: an LED is a small electric light

explanation.surface: A blade so flimsy nobody would bother carrying it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like an adjective about weight; it is the noun LED.
explanation.definitionFit: A Toledo is a fine sword made in the Spanish city famed for its steel blades.

clue.text: Mate unsettled by a blonde

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the letters of a blonde are mixed up

explanation.surface: A friend left flustered by a fair-haired woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Old bean is a dated, upper-class British form of address to a friend.

clue.text: Spouse rude at first, noble after reforming

definitions.note: in Cockney rhyming slang the phrase rhymes with and stands for wife

indicators.note: reforming means shaping again, so these letters are rearranged into new words

explanation.surface: A husband or wife began badly but improved after mending their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude at first' looks like a first-letter pick, but all of 'rude at first noble' is the fodder. Cockney rhyming slang is London dialect where a rhyming phrase replaces a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyming-slang phrase means wife, which is a kind of spouse.

clue.text: Multi-million pound agreement? I'm not impressed

definitions.meaning: a huge commercial contract or transaction
an ironic retort dismissing something as trivial

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal, a large contract; the second is the sarcastic remark 'so what?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a major transaction, and is also said sarcastically to belittle something.

clue.text: Bat makes great noise

definitions.meaning: a strung bat used in tennis or squash

explanation.definitionFit: A racket is both a tennis bat and a loud din.

clue.text: See 21
German city's basic feature: there's no church

indicators.note: there's no says the church letters are removed

parts.note: essence is the basic or intrinsic nature of something
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: What is fundamental about a German city is that it lacks a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of Germany.

clue.text: Predict early signs of unprecedented rainfall after summer month

indicators.note: after places the picked letters behind the month

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August, a summer month

indicators.note: early signs means the opening letters of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A forecaster foresees a record downpour in high summer.
explanation.definitionFit: To augur is to foretell or portend, like an ancient Roman seer reading omens.

clue.text: Greets enthusiastic supporters initially

definitions.note: greet is a Scots word meaning weep or lament

parts.note: keen means eager or enthusiastic

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of supporters is used

explanation.surface: Eager fans welcome someone at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greets' looks like a welcome, but here it is the Scots verb meaning weeps.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief, matching the Scots sense of greet, to cry.

clue.text: Woman dropped daughter off

indicators.note: off means the daughter letter is taken away

parts.note: shed means cast off or dropped

explanation.surface: A mother leaves her daughter somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped daughter off' reads as a school run; 'off' removes D from SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: The feminine pronoun refers to a woman.

clue.text: Broke in, wanting glue to sniff?

parts.note: a solvent is what glue-sniffers inhale, the volatile part of glue

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks in, looking for adhesive to inhale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke' reads as the past tense of break; it is the adjective meaning penniless. 'wanting' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to pay their debts is bankrupt, broke in the financial sense.

clue.text: Perhaps Thomas — new boy — into Moroccan food?

indicators.note: into puts the new boy inside the dish

parts.note: a tagine is a slow-cooked North African stew
Ken is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A new lad is getting into Moroccan cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thomas' is a children's-story locomotive, so 'Perhaps' marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas, the cheerful blue locomotive of children's books and TV, is an example of this steam loco.

clue.text: Some chic lady wearing dress?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stylish woman shows off her outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad means clothed, describing someone who has a garment on.
